title: Over a height-one prime with DVR localization and analytically unramified quotient, the completion is a DVR at the associated primes of the extended prime
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $R^\wedge=\varprojlim_nR/\mathfrak m^n$ its $\mathfrak m$-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Let $\mathfrak p\subset R$ be a prime ideal such that (1) the localization $R_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a discrete valuation ring, i.e. a Noetherian local integral domain whose maximal ideal $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ is generated by a single nonzero element; and (2) $\mathfrak p$ is analytically unramified [def-weil-pbc-analytically-unramified], i.e. the $(\mathfrak m/\mathfrak p)$-adic completion of the local ring $R/\mathfrak p$ is reduced. Call a prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset R^\wedge$ an associated prime of the $R^\wedge$-module $R^\wedge/\mathfrak pR^\wedge$ if $\mathfrak q=\{a\in R^\wedge: az=0\}$ for some $z\in R^\wedge/\mathfrak pR^\wedge$. Then for every such associated prime $\mathfrak q$ the localization $(R^\wedge)_{\mathfrak q}$ is a discrete valuation ring: a Noetherian local integral domain whose maximal ideal $\mathfrak q(R^\wedge)_{\mathfrak q}$ is generated by a single nonzero element.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032Z (lemma-codimension-1-analytically-unramified), lines 45889-45914 (statement and proof); tag verified in literature/stacks-project/tags/tags: 032Z,algebra-lemma-codimension-1-analytically-unramified

proof.text: Set-up. The ring $R^\wedge$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian], and the canonical map $R\to R^\wedge$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-completion-flat]. Fix an associated prime $\mathfrak q\subset R^\wedge$ of $B:=R^\wedge/\mathfrak pR^\wedge$ and put $C=(R^\wedge)_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]: a local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak qC$, and Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] (applied to $R^\wedge$ and $S=R^\wedge\setminus\mathfrak q$).

proof.text: $B=R^\wedge/\mathfrak pR^\wedge$ is a reduced ring. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-quotient] to the Noetherian local ring $(R,\mathfrak m)$ and the quotient map $\lambda:R\to R/\mathfrak p$ (kernel $J=\mathfrak p$, $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak m/\mathfrak p$): it gives a ring isomorphism $R^\wedge/\mathfrak pR^\wedge\xrightarrow{\sim}(R/\mathfrak p)^\wedge$ onto the $(\mathfrak m/\mathfrak p)$-adic completion of $R/\mathfrak p$. The latter is reduced since $\mathfrak p$ is analytically unramified (hypothesis (2), [def-weil-pbc-analytically-unramified]); a ring isomorphic to a reduced ring is reduced.

proof.text: Every $s\in R\setminus\mathfrak p$ has image outside $\mathfrak q$, hence a unit in $C$. Since $R/\mathfrak p$ is a domain, multiplication by $s$ is an injective $R$-linear map $R/\mathfrak p\to R/\mathfrak p$; tensoring with the flat $R$-module $R^\wedge$ (Step 1, [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]) keeps it injective, and $(R/\mathfrak p)\otimes_RR^\wedge\cong R^\wedge/\mathfrak pR^\wedge=B$ (right exactness of $-\otimes_RR^\wedge$ on $\mathfrak p\to R\to R/\mathfrak p\to0$), compatibly with multiplication by $s$. So $s$ is a nonzerodivisor on $B$. If $s\in\mathfrak q=\operatorname{Ann}_{R^\wedge}(\bar z)$ then $s\bar z=0$ with $\bar z\neq0$, impossible. Hence $s\notin\mathfrak q$.

proof.text:
$C$ is a discrete valuation ring. $C$ is a nonzero Noetherian local ring (Step 1) whose maximal ideal is $xC$ (Step 5) with $x$ a nonzerodivisor (Step 6); in particular $x
eq0$ in $C$ since $x\cdot1
eq0$. $C$ is a domain: $xC$ lies in the maximal ideal, which is the Jacobson radical of the local ring $C$, so [lem-weil-pbc-krull-intersection-jacobson] (ring $C$, ideal $xC$, module $C$) gives $ igcap_{n\ge0}x^nC=0$. For $a
eq0$ in $C$ there is thus a largest $n\ge0$ with $a\in x^nC$; write $a=x^nu$; then $u
otin xC$ (else $a\in x^{n+1}C$), so $u$ is a unit, $C$ being local with maximal ideal $xC$. Likewise $b=x^mv$ with $v$ a unit for $b
eq0$. Then $ab=x^{n+m}uv$, and $x^{n+m}$ is a nonzerodivisor (a product of nonzerodivisors), so $ab=0$ would give $uv=0$, impossible for a unit in the nonzero ring $C$. Hence $C$ is a Noetherian local integral domain whose maximal ideal $\mathfrak qC$ is generated by the single nonzero element $x$, i.e. a discrete valuation ring in the sense of the statement.
